newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rapeseed crop looks better than expected.
newsitem.headline: French rapeseed crop looks better than expected.

text.p: The French rapeseed harvest is 60-70 percent complete and initial results suggest that with the exception of the drought-hit south, the crop fared much better than expected.
A crop analyst for French oilseeds institute Cetiom said the national yield could reach 3.0-3.3 tonnes per hectare in 1997 against a record 3.3 tonnes last year.
"This is a nice surprise. It is much better than we thought," he said.
In the southwest and the southeast, where the harvest is now over, yields were hit by a prolonged drought in the spring.
Farmers there are reporting yields as low as 2.4-2.5 tonnes per hectare.

But the main production regions of centre France, Burgundy and Franche Comte, where the harvest is now 70 percent complete, show yields of 3.1-3.2 tonnes as rain in May and June helped the crop recoup damages.
In the Poitou Charentes early cuts also suggest yields could exceed 3.0 tonnes per hectare, the analyst said.
North of the Loire river, rain delayed the start of the harvest by about a week and raised fears quality might be hit.
But with the exception of a few cases of unwanted germination in centre France, the rain had no impact on quality, the analyst said.
In its July report the farm ministry forecast yields might decline to 2.97 tonnes in 1997 from a record 3.3 tonnes in 1996.
Assuming a 9.6 percent rise in rapeseed sowing to 959,000 hectares, the ministry had forecast a 2.3 percent drop in the rapeseed crop to 2.847 million tonnes.
But the Cetiom analyst said the ministry was likely to revise upwards its yield estimate in its next report.
